issues.body: contexts_from_pairs reads indices 0 and 1 but does not check pair.length() == 2. Thus [url, documentText, extra] is accepted even though the function and public API documentation say malformed entries that are not two-string arrays are rejected. The wasm malformed-input test covers a non-array and a short pair, but still does not cover an overlong pair. This is materially the same minor finding as round 1.
issues.fix_hint: Reject pairs unless pair.length() == 2 and add a wasm test asserting that an overlong pair is rejected, or explicitly document that only the first two elements are consumed and extras are ignored.
issues.title: Context entries still are not validated to contain exactly two elements

verdict.summary: The feature remains opt-in, fail-closed, and covered on both the native parsing path and the real wasm boundary. However, the sole round-1 validation mismatch remains unchanged: contexts_from_pairs still reads only elements 0 and 1 without requiring pair.length() == 2, so an overlong entry is accepted despite the documented exact two-element shape. Because this is the same minor contract/documentation issue and no blocker or major correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security defect is evident, approval remains appropriate.
